quiz.q: How does NAFTA fundamentally differ from regional integration blocs like the European Union?
options: It establishes a shared political parliament and common currency across all member states.
It is strictly a commercial trading bloc without any supranational governing institutions.
It requires member nations to merge their sovereign defence and foreign policy structures.
It operates as a unified customs union with a single common external tariff.
quiz.why: NAFTA was created purely as a commercial trading bloc and intentionally lacks any supranational governing institutions like those found in the European Union.

quiz.q: Under NAFTA, what is the primary function of the 'rules of origin' clause?
options: To mandate that all imported manufactured goods originate entirely from developing member nations.
To allow non-member nations to freely export assembled automobiles into North American markets.
To require member states to completely equalize their domestic industrial wages and taxes.
To ensure products contain substantial member-country content before receiving duty-free trade benefits.
quiz.why: Rules of origin require exported goods to contain a substantial percentage of member-country components to qualify for tariff-free benefits.

quiz.q: According to the class notes, what was the primary driver of President Trump's opposition to NAFTA?
options: Domestic electoral politics aimed at winning working-class voters hurt by factory job relocations.
A catastrophic decline in North American trade competitiveness against European and Asian economies.
Canada's refusal to supply crude oil and agricultural commodities to United States markets.
Mexico's complete rejection of United States intellectual property and dispute settlement mechanisms.
quiz.why: Opposition to NAFTA was driven by domestic political calculations to win over working-class voters who lost industrial manufacturing jobs.

quiz.q: Why do the notes conclude that NAFTA faces no real existential threat despite strong political attacks?
options: The World Trade Organization legally prohibits member states from renegotiating regional free trade treaties.
All member countries have fully integrated their national currencies into a single North American system.
United States economic gains, stable energy imports, and counterbalancing China outweigh political complaints.
Mexico and Canada agreed to absorb all manufacturing wage differences across the three borders.
quiz.why: The strategic benefits of low energy costs and collective competitiveness against Chinese influence make NAFTA too advantageous for the United States to abandon.
